description: An XDCR replication's status is documented with three different value sets on three surfaces, and no page reconciles them. (1) Capella's Web UI, in cloud/clusters/xdcr/manage-xdcr-replications.md, lists seven: 'Replication status can be 1 of the following' - Creating, Active, Pausing, Paused, Deleting, Create Error, Delete Error. (2) The Server Web Console's XDCR screen shows two, in server/8.0/manage/manage-xdcr/pause-xdcr-replication.md and resume-xdcr-replication.md: 'the **status** column displays a status of `replicating`' and 'this replication is shown as `paused`'. (3) The Server REST API's cluster-tasks array, in server/8.0/rest-api/rest-xdcr-adv-settings.md, reports an XDCR task as `"status": "running"` and does not model pause as a status value at all - it carries a separate `"pauseRequested": false` boolean alongside it. So the same lifecycle is 'Active' in one place, `replicating` in another and `running` in a third; pause is a status on two surfaces and a request flag on the third; and only Capella documents error states. A reader or a tool moving between the Capella UI, the Server UI and the REST API has no mapping to work from, and nothing tells them one is needed.
note: Filed rather than modelled. The registry holds xdcr:replication-status-enum as an explicit DIVERGENCE record - three files use the id, each documenting a different value set - and promoting a value list would assert an agreement that does not exist. This is also the round's one candidate-evidence.py --audit finding: the id's original round-7 evidence string elided the Capella table with '...' and so was not literally quotable from its page. Re-reading cloud/clusters/xdcr/manage-xdcr-replications.md lines 341-352 confirmed the seven statuses are genuinely there in table form, so the flag was an elision artefact rather than fabrication - but checking it is what turned up the REST surface's different SHAPE, which nobody had noticed.
